blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Local feature matching is typically formulated for image pairs, although structure-from-motion and visual localization commonly match one reference image against many retrieved or covisible neighbours. Applying a pairwise matcher independently to these centre-neighbour edges duplicates reference-side computation and prevents the matcher from exploiting complementary multi-view geometric evidence from the remaining observations. To address these limitations, we introduce MVLoMa, a sparse star-graph matcher that extends LoMa from image pairs to multiple views. MVLoMa first uses a frozen multi-view geometry model to jointly describe all images in a star, then injects the resulting cross-view geometric context into local descriptors. It then matches the centre image to all neighbours in a single forward pass through per-view self-attention and bidirectional centre-neighbour cross-attention. For supervision, we derive positive correspondences only from depth-valid, mutually visible dense warps and explicitly penalize high-confidence matches that violate epipolar geometry. On 25-view star graphs from HyperSim, ScanNet++, Mip-NeRF 360, and Tanks and Temples, MVLoMa obtains the best macro-average relative-pose AUC among the compared methods at all three thresholds (58.65/85.41/90.99). Its matcher is 2.20 times faster than sequential evaluation of the 24 centre-neighbour edges. The same design supports four tested frozen geometry encoders -- DA3, $π^3$, VGGT, and VGGT-$Ω$ -- with DA3-Giant performing best on all reported encoder-ablation metrics. Controlled ablations further isolate the effects of geometry-aware descriptors, visibility filtering, geometric negative supervision, and joint multi-view inference.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Reliable correspondence is the interface through which images become
geometric constraints. It underlies camera pose estimation, mapping, visual
localization, and structure-from-motion (SfM). Learned sparse
matchers ( Sarlin et al., 2020 ; Lindenberger et al., 2023 ; Nordström et al., 2026 ) combine local descriptors with contextual assignment, while detector-free
and dense methods predict a broader set of
correspondences ( Sun et al., 2021 ; Edstedt et al., 2024 ; Edstedt et al., 2026 ) .
This progress has made two-view pose estimation substantially more robust.
Yet it also leaves a mismatch between the unit of computation used by a
matcher—an image pair—and the unit of evidence available to downstream
geometry—a group of mutually overlapping images.

blocks.en:
Consider the ubiquitous star graph: a reference image and its retrieved
neighbours. This topology occurs when SfM builds local subproblems, when
localization matches a query to a covisible map neighbourhood, and when a
keyframe associates observations over time. A pairwise matcher is invoked
once for every reference–neighbour edge. It consequently recomputes the
reference descriptor and reference-side matcher branch, and it must decide
each correspondence before seeing supporting or conflicting evidence from
the remaining neighbours. The limitation is not merely redundant
computation. Repetitive texture, partial occlusion, and a weak baseline can
make a match ambiguous in one pair while a third image resolves the
ambiguity.

Existing multi-view matchers move contextualization from isolated pairs to
collaborative groups or tracks ( Zhang et al., 2025 ; Lee et al., 2026 ) .
However, their dense or groupwise outputs are not designed for the repeated
sparse centre–neighbour assignments of a star graph. Simply batching
pairwise matchers preserves that sparse interface but prevents communication
between edges. We therefore seek a matcher that reasons jointly over a star
while retaining explicit pairwise outputs for RANSAC.

There is a second, largely independent source of unused information. Recent
3D foundation models predict pose, depth, and geometry from arbitrary view
collections by exchanging information across image
tokens ( Wang et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026b ; Lin et al., 2025 ) . Their spatially aligned
final-layer tokens already encode multi-view geometric context, yet local
matching commonly starts from a separate frozen 2D descriptor backbone.
Reusing these tokens exposes geometry to the matcher without introducing
another frozen feature stream. Keeping the foundation encoder fixed also
avoids optimizing its large parameter set and preserves a reusable geometric
representation.

These observations suggest a simple principle: jointly match a star
once, and reuse the frozen geometric representation that the star has
already produced . We instantiate this principle in MVLoMa , a multi-view
extension of LoMa ( Nordström et al., 2026 ) . A light trainable descriptor

frozen 3D foundation encoder. A star-structured matcher then shares the
centre representation across all edges and alternates per-view
self-attention with bidirectional centre–neighbour cross-attention. It
outputs a conventional score matrix for every edge, so its matches can be
consumed directly by standard robust pose estimation.

Our experiments follow a 25-view star-graph protocol and evaluate the same

remains stronger on Mip-NeRF 360 at the strictest threshold, while MVLoMa provides a sparse multi-view alternative that operates on all 25 views in

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Sparse and Dense Feature Matching
blocks.zh: 2.1 花样和花样匹配

blocks.en:
Local matching has evolved from independently comparing hand-designed
features to learned descriptor and assignment pipelines. SuperGlue
contextualizes detected keypoints with graph
attention ( Sarlin et al., 2020 ) ; LightGlue improves the same family
with adaptive depth and pruning ( Lindenberger et al., 2023 ) . LoFTR
removes the detector by matching coarse image features ( Sun et al., 2021 ) .
In parallel, RoMa and RoMa v2 obtain robust dense correspondence from
foundation features and coarse-to-fine
refinement ( Edstedt et al., 2024 ; Edstedt et al., 2026 ) . LoMa shows that a
carefully scaled local-feature recipe remains highly
competitive ( Nordström et al., 2026 ) . These methods differ in sparsity and
representation, but their assignment is fundamentally pairwise. MVLoMa inherits LoMa’s local descriptor refinement and dual-softmax interface while
moving contextual reasoning from an image pair to a star graph.

blocks.en: 2.2 Multi-View Correspondence and Tracks
blocks.zh: 2.2 多维通信和跟踪

blocks.en:
Multi-view information has long been used after matching to merge pairwise
correspondences into tracks. More recent learned methods use it inside the
matcher. CoMatcher employs groupwise interaction to make keypoint matching
collaborative ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) , whereas MV-RoMa aggregates dense
multi-view correspondence into tracks ( Lee et al., 2026 ) . These
approaches establish that complementary observations can reduce pairwise
ambiguity. Our setting is deliberately more structured: a star has one
centre whose features participate in every output edge. We therefore use a
centre–neighbour communication pattern rather than full
neighbour–neighbour interaction. The resulting model retains a score matrix
and confidence for each individual edge, enabling the usual sparse matching
and RANSAC interface without a post-hoc track snapping stage.

blocks.en:
DUSt3R and MASt3R learn feedforward geometric representations from image
pairs ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Leroy et al., 2024 ) . VGGT, π 3 \pi^{3} , and DA3 extend
the input from pairs to view collections and exchange token information
across views ( Wang et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026b ; Lin et al., 2025 ) . These models are
typically used to decode camera and scene geometry, while a separate
matching system constructs explicit correspondences. We instead ask whether
their last-layer, cross-view-fused tokens can serve as a frozen
geometry-aware input to a sparse matcher. This choice is distinct from
directly decoding tracks with a foundation model: it preserves a specialized
assignment head and leaves the geometry encoder unchanged.

blocks.en:
Optimization-based SfM obtains global geometry by matching image pairs,
building tracks, and geometrically verifying
them ( Schönberger and Frahm, 2016 ; Pan et al., 2024 ) . Hybrid systems couple
these explicit constraints with feedforward geometry
priors ( Duisterhof et al., 2025 ; Pan et al., 2026 ) . They motivate star
subgraphs as a scalable local unit, but the correspondence module is still
often assembled from independent pairwise matchers or heterogeneous track
sources. MVLoMa addresses this upstream bottleneck; it is a matching
primitive rather than a replacement for global optimization.

attention workload without providing a direct output edge. We therefore use
the star topology itself as the attention pattern

blocks.en:
The attention pattern establishes how evidence is exchanged; supervision
must ensure that this evidence is geometrically meaningful. We obtain
LoMa-style positive correspondences by reprojecting ground-truth depth with
ground-truth pose. A naive dense warp, however, treats occluded,
out-of-image, and invalid-depth pixels as if they had a valid target.

its source depth is valid, its reprojection lies inside the target image,
and the prescribed occlusion and target-depth consistency checks are
satisfied. This filtering removes label noise before it reaches either the
descriptor or the assignment head.

blocks.en:
We describe the architecture, loss, evaluation topology, RANSAC setting,
keypoint budget, frozen/trainable components, and reported training
schedules in the main paper, with further detail in
Appendix A . The method builds directly on publicly
available LoMa-style matching components and multi-view 3D foundation
encoders. We will release the implementation and evaluation configuration
upon publication.

blocks.en:
MVLoMa depends on the geometric quality of the frozen foundation features;
textureless or uncertain regions can still yield sparse or ambiguous
matches. The centre–neighbour topology does not directly exchange
information between neighbours, and the memory requirement still grows with
the number of keypoints and views. Our 2–8-view training range is also
smaller than the 25-view evaluation star. Although the view-count ablation
shows useful extrapolation, it is not uniformly monotonic and does not
establish that all additional observations are beneficial. Learning view
selection or confidence-aware neighbour aggregation is a promising direction
for larger stars. Finally, we evaluate the matcher through relative pose
estimation; its interaction with complete global SfM systems is outside the
scope of this work.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We presented MVLoMa to resolve a mismatch in current geometric pipelines:
pairwise assignment discards evidence and foundation features that are
already available across a view collection. MVLoMa reuses frozen
geometry-aware tokens and shares the centre representation across a star,
while preserving ordinary sparse pairwise outputs for robust pose
estimation. Across four benchmarks, the 784 model attains the strongest
macro-average AUC among the compared methods at all three thresholds, and
its 25-view matcher is 2.20 × 2.20\times faster than sequential pairwise
evaluation. The ablations further show that the gains depend on both the
frozen representation and the proposed supervision, while the non-monotonic
view-count results clarify that additional context is useful but not
uniformly beneficial.
